title: What does the XRPL PasswordSpent account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of PasswordSpent and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, PasswordSpent records whether an account has used its free regular-key reset transaction. [1]

This is an AccountRoot state flag with no matching AccountSet toggle. It must not be treated as a web password status, a seed-exposure signal or a general permission to reset signing authority without cost. The account still needs a valid signing method. Inspect current signing configuration and transaction-cost rules when planning a regular-key change. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for PasswordSpent and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why PasswordSpent is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
